newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee market paralysed by price rises.
newsitem.headline: German coffee market paralysed by price rises.

text.p: German green coffee buyers are sidelined in a market dominated by supply tightness and the possibility of further price rises, traders said on Monday.
"It's a dangerous market in which roasters are unwilling to pay current prices and where some traders are extremely short," one trader said.
"Even if futures have reached their peak, the question is where will the coffee for the second half of 1997 come from."
Arabicas soared in New York last Friday as traders dismissed a bearish 1997/98 Brazil crop forecast.
May closed at 176.85 cents/lb, up 5.75, and a squeeze is looming on March, which ended up 7.30 cents at 190.40.
A fall in certified New York coffee stocks after the close lent short-term support.
"It is hard to give roasters sensible advice at the moment, when the entire sector is grappling with tight availability and firm differentials," one trader said.
In the domestic market, retail price increases are due to come into effect later this month as roasters seek to pass on higher raw materials costs and the additional burden of the strong dollar.
But many fear a negative consumer reaction.
In the northern German import markets, trades were thin as arabica prices jumped $8-10 per 50 kg fob on the week.
Brazils were at $187 fob, up $8, but differentials eased relative to other origins.
Vietnam robustas were up $4 at $72 cif.
